$comment: The reusable-workflow graphs for the D1 controls, as data.
They live here rather than in reusable-workflow-controls.py for a structural
reason. Every filename in boundary.INVENTORY is a token local_script_closure
resolves, so naming a module there puts it in the retention workflow's script
closure, and publication_policy then reads its text as the workflow's own
capability. A control module carrying a literal `packages: write`, an `oras`
push or a `secrets:` reference would fail the pristine tree. Data files are
not scripts and are never walked. The alternative -- adding the module to
boundary.POLICY_SELF -- would widen the one exemption in this design a
reviewer should be attacking, and is not worth a string.
`caller` is always written to .github/workflows/caller.yml inside a throwaway
tree; `files` are written beside it. `expect` is the property the control must
reach, and null means the graph must be accepted.
readOnlyPreamble:
name: Called
on:
  workflow_call:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  work:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Do nothing that can publish
        shell: bash
        run: echo 'this workflow holds no grant and no credential'

controls.name: 01-called-workflow-holds-packages-write
controls.property: a local reusable workflow granting packages: write is refused
controls.caller:
name: Caller
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  delegate:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml

files..github/workflows/called.yml:
name: Called
on:
  workflow_call:
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
jobs:
  work:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo hello

controls.name: 02-called-workflow-logs-in-and-pushes
controls.property: a local reusable workflow performing a registry login and push is refused
controls.caller:
name: Caller
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  delegate:

files..github/workflows/called.yml:
name: Called
on:
  workflow_call:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  work:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Publish
        shell: bash
        run: |
          oras login ghcr.io --password-stdin
          oras manifest push ghcr.io/tesserafin-project/windows-ffmpeg-runtime@sha256:0 manifest.json
